summary: The root خشي primarily signifies fear, particularly a reverential fear or awe of God. It implies being humbled and submissive due to this fear, often leading to avoidance of what is feared.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: aor. يَخْشَى, inf. n. خَشْيَةٌ (JK, S, M, Msb, K) and خَشْىٌ (JK, M, K) and خِشْىٌ (Sgh, K) [the second and third erroneously written in the CK خَشًا and (by indication) خِشًا ] and خَشَاةٌ (M, K) and خَشْيَانٌ, (JK, M, K,) though it has been said that the only instances of this kind are شَنْآنٌ and لَيَّانٌ, [see the former of these two,] but in one copy of the M found written خِشْيَانٌ, (TA,) and مَخْشَاةٌ (JK, M, K) and مَخْشِيَةٌ, (M, K,) He feared; syn.

inf. n. تَخْشِيَةٌ, He frightened him, or made him to fear; (S, K;) [or he made him to dread; or to fear with reverence, &c.; (see 1;)] بِالأَمْرِ [ with the thing, or event ]. (TA.) One says, خَشِّ ُؤَالَةَ بِالحِبَالَةِ, meaning [ Frighten thou ] the wolf [with the snare]. (S. [See art. أل.]) And لَقَدْ كُنْتُ وَمَا أُخَشَّى بِال ِّئْبِ [ Verily I used to be in a state when I was not frightened by the wolf ]: a prov. (JK, TA.)

خَاْشَىَ خَاشَانِى, (A'Obeyd, S, K,) aor. of the latter أَخْشِيهِ, (A'Obeyd, S,) [ I vied with him in fear or dread, and ] I was more fearful [or dreading ] than he. (A 'Obeyed, S, K.) خَاشَى فُلَانًا, (JK, TA,) inf. n. مُخَاشَاةٌ, (TA,) He left, forsook, relinquished, or abandoned, such a one, being left, &c., by him. (JK, TA.) خاشى بِهِمْ He guarded himself against them in an extraordinary degree, and was cautious, or wary, (JK, TA,) and therefore turned away, or withdrew. (TA.)

Fearful, or fearing; (S, Msb, TA;) [or dreading; i. e. fearing with reverence, &c.: (see 1:)] as also and: (K:) fem. خَشْيَا, (S, Msb, K, [in the CK, erroneously, خَشْيَآءُ,]) like غَضْبَى fem, of غَضْبَانُ, (Msb,) accord. to rule, (TA,) and خَشْيَانَةٌ, mentioned by El- arzookee, and thought by MF to be of the dial. of Asad; (TA;) or this signifies a wo man who fears, or dreads, ( تَخْشَى,) everything; (JK, TA;) so in the Tekmileh: (TA:) pl.
Land such as is termed جَهَادٌ [i. e. hard; or having no herbage; or hard, and having no herbage; or level; or rugged, &c.]. (JK, Sgh, K.)

Dry; (As, JK, S, K;) like حَشِىٌّ; (As, S;) applied to herbage; (As, S;) or to herbs and trees: (JK:) or dry and rotten. (IAar, TA.) A rájiz says, (S,) namely, Sakhr, (TA,) سَمُّ َرَارِيحَ رِطَابٍ وَخَشِىْ [ Poison of moist cantharides, and dry ]; (S, TA;) meaning وَخَشِىٍّ, suppressing one of the two ى s by poetic license. (IB, TA.)

meaning More [and most ] fearful, or feared, [or dreaded, ] (S, K,) is anomalous, (K,) being from the pass. [verb, like its syn. أَخْوَفُ ]. (TA.) You say, هٰ َا المَكَانُ أَخْشَى مِنْ َاكَ This place is more fearful, or feared, [or dreaded, ] than that. (S, K. *)
[pl. of مَخْشَاةٌ, originally مَخْشَيَةٌ,] Causes of fear [or dread ]; syn. مَخَاوِفُ [pl. of مَخَافَةٌ: like which, مَخْشَاةٌ is also an inf. n.]. (Har p. 138.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
